extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students and instructors of English literature; readers studying Matthew Arnold and principles of criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and presents Matthew Arnold's standards for literary criticism, style, and the relation of culture to criticism; aimed at guiding how to judge and practice criticism, poetry, and prose. Emphasizes virtues of the critic, stylistic qualities, and cultural aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism is "the disinterested endeavor to learn and propagate the best that is known and thought in the world," with the ultimate purpose "to keep man from a self-satisfaction which is retarding and vulgarizing, to lead him towards perfection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism is not confined to art and literature but includes society, politics, and religion; it should both censure faults and appreciate/popularize the best.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness (freedom from partisanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Foremost of these is disinterestedness." The critic should avoid partisanship; knowing a person's 'sect' biases anticipated argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from active participation in politics, social or humanitarian work when possible; partisanship blinds the critic and undermines clearness of vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: The critical effort is "the effort to see the object as in itself it really is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach truth from as many ways and sides as possible to avoid narrowness and mistaken judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of abstract systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid abstract systems "which petrify and hinder the necessary flexibility of mind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain intellectual flexibility; do not let rigid doctrinal frameworks dictate judgment or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coolness of temper
rubrics_metrics.description: Coolness is enjoined: "It is only by remaining collected ... that the critic can do the practical man any service"; preserve "sweetness and good humor," even in ridicule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain collectedness and measured tone; temper harshness with civility so critique can be useful and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endeavor to understand and sympathize
rubrics_metrics.description: Critic should "endeavor to understand, to sympathize with, and to guide intelligently the main tendencies of his age, rather than violently to oppose them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor comprehension and guidance over outright denunciation; present remedies courageously but reasonably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage to present unpleasant antidotes
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must have "the courage to present unpleasant antidotes to [the age's] faults" and not foster conceit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to give corrective, even unpopular advice when necessary, balancing sympathy with frankness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith in spiritual progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain "a high faith in spiritual progress and an unwavering belief that the ideal life is 'the normal life as we shall one day see it.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical work should be motivated by constructive optimism about moral and cultural improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style grounded in character; limpidness and simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Style's basis is character; Arnold values "limpidness," "simplicity," "lucidity," clearness and effectiveness as the transparent quality of true style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for transparency so the writer's basic character and thought shine through; favor clear, simple expression over ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness through crystallized phrases (use of apothegms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystallize thought into telling phrases (e.g., "Philistinism," "sweetness and light," "the grand style").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such phrases aid clarity and memorability, but beware the danger of letting succinct apothegms substitute for complex truth; risk of oversimplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of emotionalism and rhapsody
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not indulge in emotionalism or rhythmical prose; though occasional poetic quality may appear, avoid rhapsodic writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quiet, deep feeling and controlled expression rather than excessive rhetorical flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor used as deliberate, secondary weapon
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is "almost too conscious" and appears as "playful satire"—a literary weapon directed toward serious purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use humor sparingly and purposefully to illuminate or correct, not as an end in itself; avoid undermining seriousness when inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and particular representation in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing on Aristotle: "Any representation therefore which is consistently drawn may be supposed to be interesting... What is not interesting is that which does not add to our knowledge... that which is vaguely conceived and loosely drawn."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer particularity, precision, and firmness in depiction; avoid vague, indeterminate, or loose portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical ideal of composition (fit details for a noble general result)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical art is prized for "fit details strictly combined, in view of a large general result nobly conceived"—clarity, harmony, and wholeness of effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize details so they serve a unified, noble whole; favor classical balance and unity over disordered eclecticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as instrument for humanization
rubrics_metrics.description: Arnold holds that "poetry is our best instrument for humanization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use poetry (and poetic qualities in prose) to cultivate refinement, moral depth, and the 'humanizing' of readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture as 'a study of perfection' and critic's role as apostle
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture is "a study of perfection." The critic is the "appointed apostle of culture," seeking out and ministering to the means of self-improvement and propagating the best known and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue and propagate the best intellectual and spiritual attainments; culture implies both personal perfection and its sharing with others (propagation, increased sympathy, sweetness, light, life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confining culture to mere classical smattering
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture is not "a smattering of Greek and Latin," but a deepening and strengthening of the whole spiritual nature by all means at our command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize genuine breadth and depth of cultivation rather than superficial erudition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detachment and self-culture (value of aloofness)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Goethe: value of detachment—"aloofness, provided it be not selfish"—useful to watch life's struggles calmly and to find refuge in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a reflective distance that allows judgment and self-culture without selfish disengagement from duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and self-dependence (Stoic influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus: look within for "the aids to noble life," learn to resign passionate hopes "for quiet and a fearless mind," and merge self in obedience to universal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a disciplined inner life and moral steadiness that informs critical judgments and creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt style and scope of exposition to readers' familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: "How much space shall be devoted to exposition, and how much to illustration, depends largely on the familiarity of his subject to his readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust balance between explanation and example according to audience knowledge; be pedagogically patient when readers need it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of pseudo-classicism and overreaction to movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Arnold finds shallowness in pseudo-classicism (e.g., Pope) and rejects extremes of romanticism, aiming for the strengths of Greek clarity and modern depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique movements and styles by seeking their genuine merits and faults; adopt a balanced stance rather than wholesale acceptance or rejection.
